summary: Moon River is a song composed by Henry Mancini with lyrics by Johnny Mercer, originally performed by Audrey Hepburn in the 1961 film Breakfast at Tiffany's. It won an Academy Award for Best Original Song and the 1962 Grammy Awards for Record of the Year and Song of the Year. The note explains that Mercer's lyrics draw on his Savannah, Georgia childhood and how the lyrics first appear in the film, when Paul Varjak discovers Holly Golightly singing it on a fire escape.
one_line: A 1961 song by Henry Mancini and Johnny Mercer, sung by Audrey Hepburn in Breakfast at Tiffany's, with lyrics drawn from Mercer's Savannah childhood.
key_facts: Moon River is a song composed by Henry Mancini with lyrics by Johnny Mercer.
Moon River was originally performed by Audrey Hepburn in the 1961 movie Breakfast at Tiffany's.
Moon River won an Academy Award for Best Original Song.
Moon River won the 1962 Grammy Awards for Record of the Year and Song of the Year.
Henry Mancini and Johnny Mercer wrote Moon River for Audrey Hepburn to sing in Breakfast at Tiffany's.
The lyrics of Moon River, written by Johnny Mercer, are reminiscent of his childhood in Savannah, Georgia, including its waterways.
As a child, Johnny Mercer picked huckleberries in summer, which he connected with a carefree childhood and Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn.
An instrumental version of Moon River is played over the opening titles of Breakfast at Tiffany's.
The lyrics of Moon River are first heard in a scene where Paul Varjak (George Peppard) discovers Holly Golightly (Audrey Hepburn) singing the song.
In the scene where the lyrics are first heard, Holly Golightly accompanies herself on the guitar while sitting on the fire escape outside their apartments.
